s: weaver (male or of unspecified gender) (someone who weaves); webster
weaver (as a component part of multiple compound names, mainly various bird (or other animal) species)
Weber.et: From Middle High German webære, from Old High German weberi, equivalent to weben (“to weave”) + -er. Cognate with Luxembourgish Wiewer, English weaver.

s: a common surname originating as an occupation
Weber.et: From Middle High German webære, from Old High German weberi, equivalent to weben (“to weave”) + -er. Cognate with Luxembourgish Wiewer, English weaver.
Named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard Weber

s: to sway back and forth, to swing, to ramble
weben.et: From Middle High German weben, from Old High German weban, from Proto-West Germanic *weban. Compare Dutch weven, English weave, Danish væve.

Webseite.et: Web + Seite (“page”), calque of English web page.

Webinar.et: Unadapted borrowing from English webinar, though also independently analyzable as a blend of Web and Seminar.

Webbrowser.et: Unadapted borrowing from English web browser. Equivalent to Web + Browser.

s: Activity on the Internet, i.e. one's digital footprint.
Webpräsenz.et: From web + Präsenz (presence), in the same vein as Internetpräsenz.
